in_support_vs_att.interpretation: ATT is lower-is-better, so a POSITIVE correlation means the in-support fraction ranks the targets BACKWARDS. This is reported as a result: the criterion BRIEF_15 section 5 originally allowed to select a rule is anti-correlated with the outcome it was meant to proxy, which is why its withdrawal (section 12.1) was necessary rather than merely cautious, and which is evidence that conditioning outside the training support is the mechanism operating as designed rather than a defect

probe.best_source_return_meaning: the maximum episode return of the training split -- the naive rule's target, and R_best_source in Rule B
probe.return_definition: per-intersection episode return under the collection reward, summed over the post-step infos of one episode; verified against -sum(lane_waiting over the intersection's incoming lanes) on every episode
probe.role: the in-domain MaxPressure probe: the input to both calibration rules, and the source-domain half of Rule B's ratio that P7 consumes

rules.rule_a: target = quantile(probe returns); the DECLARED ALTERNATIVE, predicted before the run to be poor because it targets probe-achievable rather than best-achievable return
rules.rule_b: target = best_source x (probe_target_stat / probe_source_stat); THE MECHANISM. In domain the two statistics coincide, the ratio is exactly 1 and the rule returns the naive target, so this task asserts the identity and measures the source-domain half of the ratio rather than validating the rule

role: P4.3's RTG landscape on the registered held-out pool: the declared grid, the naive rule's position on it, Rule A as the declared alternative, and the in-support reliability diagnostic. EXPLORATORY (PREREGISTRATION.md section 2): effect sizes and CIs, no inferential claim, no multiplicity correction
